sceneDescriptions.jade: You are entering the deer's sanctuary. At the center of a great carved stone disc, a stag stands still in the dry grass, maize around him. This is the hearth, the centre the four directions run from: the gold of dawn to the east, the turquoise of noon to the south, the red of dusk to the west, the violet of night to the north. The deer is your nahual: the essence revealed in animal form.
sceneDescriptions.dore: You face the East, Tlahuizcalpan, the house of dawn. The world is caught in the frost of Itztlacoliuhqui, the stag under ice, time stopped. When the sun appears, the darts of dawn fly and all the ice shatters. The light is new, the day opens.
sceneDescriptions.turquoise: You face the South, Huitztlampa, land of thorns and flowers. Huitzilopochtli watches over what grows. The scene takes on turquoise tones of Xiuhtecuhtli mosaic.
sceneDescriptions.cendre: You face the West, Cihuatlampa, region of the mauve twilight. The Cihuateteo, deified dead women, carry the setting sun in a litter of feathers, then come down to the crossroads and dance in the wind. The scene glows softly red, then goes dark.
sceneDescriptions.obsidienne: You face the North, Mictlampa, the place of rest. Mictlantecuhtli, lord of violet obsidian, keeps what has been lived. The scene turns nocturnal, deep.

home.heroText: Among the Nahua, a Mesoamerican people, the deer (Mazātl) is the seventh day of the sacred calendar: a messenger between worlds, associated with grace, vigilance, and the ability to hide its true nature from others. The nahual is the same idea: a human essence revealed in its true animal form, embodied here by this deer.
home.aboutText:
Nahual, the studio, applies the same logic to the web: turning an idea into a real, working site. The proof it worked? It works for everyone.

Sylvain Maurier, senior frontend developer, 10 years of experience (React, Next.js, Vue/Nuxt, React Native). Specialized in digital accessibility (RGAA/WCAG), with one simple conviction: accessibility is built, not just audited.

chapters.line: He grazes in the half-light, indifferent to the path leading toward him.
The stag has noticed you. He doesn't flee · he waits.
A silence. Three entities: your body, his body, what passes between them.
Four directions around you, a fifth at the center. Yours to choose.
You move. The world trembles. The journey begins.

services.title: Services
services.intro: Nahual is Sylvain Maurier's creative studio, a senior frontend developer specialized in digital accessibility. Two offers, one goal: websites that work, for everyone.

webCard.title: Website development
webCard.text: Showcase sites, custom applications: frontend and fullstack development (React, Next.js, Vue/Nuxt), design systems, performance. From spec to launch.

auditCard.title: RGAA accessibility audit
auditCard.text: RGAA/WCAG compliance audits with directly implementable recommendations. I deliver the fix code, not just a report.
auditCard.note: Certification in progress (access42 exam, October 23, 2026), not yet obtained.

projets.title: Projects
projets.intro: Four recent projects. Deep case studies rather than a gallery of screenshots.

nuada.title: Nuada · RGAA accessibility audit
nuada.text: Showcase site and RGAA audit engine. WCAG 2.2 compliance, multilingual SEO, positioned as "the auditor who codes the fix."
nuada.context: The French RGAA audit market is saturated with PDF reports no one knows how to implement. Nuada was built around a simple idea: deliver the fix code, not just the diagnosis.
nuada.role: Product owner, art direction, complete development. Solo builder.
nuada.stack: Astro, TypeScript, MDX, native i18n fr/en/es, Netlify hosting.
nuada.highlights: Rare positioning against classic firms ("the auditor who codes"). Public transparent pricing grid. Quick online audit demo on submitted URL.
nuada.outcome: Live since August 2026. First conversations with 3 prospects between September and October.

detail.hero: The auditor who codes the fix.

narrative.title: The market reality
narrative.text: The French RGAA accessibility audit market is mature but paradoxical. Large firms deliver 80-page PDF reports, structured against the 106 criteria of the standard, listing each non-compliance with a screenshot and a generic recommendation. The engineering teams receiving those reports are often left helpless: how do you translate "improve link focus contrast" into a concrete pull request? Nuada starts from that observation to propose something else.

narrative.title: The technical stance
narrative.text: Each non-compliance identified by Nuada is delivered with directly implementable fix code, tested on a client project fork when possible. No vague "recommendation," no "to investigate on the team side": a Git diff, an explanation of why, a non-regression test. The auditor becomes a temporary contributor, not a consultant leaving behind a knot of problems.

narrative.title: Site architecture
narrative.text: Astro for static generation, native i18n for fr/en/es with no overhead, MDX for long-form articles, Netlify hosting with preview branches for each new piece of content. The site itself is RGAA 4.1 compliant by construction · no post-audit patching, every component is designed accessible from the start. A test-driven a11y approach that serves as its own example.

narrative.title: What Nuada teaches me
narrative.text: Building Nuada forced me to formalize what was implicit: what I did intuitively on client missions (deliver code rather than text) becomes a reproducible method. The real deliverable of an accessibility audit isn't a document, it's a codebase more accessible than before.

narrative.title: Next steps
narrative.text: Once the RGAA certification is validated (access42 exam October 23, 2026), Nuada can move from showcase site to real tool: partial audit automation via axe-core in CI, before/after comparator on pull request, public library of reusable accessible patterns.

kleyfrance.title: KleyFrance
kleyfrance.text: Full WordPress site rebuild + logo creation for a manufacturer of custom lifting solutions (oil, offshore, military).
kleyfrance.context: Aging site, not responsive, no visual charter. International B2B target with demanding, very technical vocabulary (slinging, marine winches, LOLER).
kleyfrance.role: Art direction, logo creation, WordPress custom theme rebuild.
kleyfrance.stack: WordPress, ACF Pro, responsive custom theme, subtle GSAP animations.
kleyfrance.highlights: Industrial visual charter without falling into "heavy metal" cliché. Product photothèque organized by sector (naval / offshore / defense). B2B multilingual SEO.
kleyfrance.outcome: Site live, loading time cut by 3, mobile-friendly, unified quote forms.

detail.hero: Making a niche industrial site breathe.

narrative.title: Client context
narrative.text: KleyFrance is a French manufacturer of custom lifting solutions · slings, winches, specialized spreader beams · for very specialized sectors: oil, offshore oceanography, military industry. A legacy WordPress site, not responsive, whose graphic charter came down to an aging logo and a gray-blue palette without identity. The brief: rebuild while keeping industrial credibility, without falling into the "heavy metal" cliché that plagues this market.

narrative.title: Art direction approach
narrative.text: Rather than a flashy site, a design that breathes technical seriousness. Product photos on a clean background, sober but modern industrial typography (not thick futura, rather a balanced neo-grotesque), tight palette deep blue + functional orange like a safety marking ribbon. The redesigned logo keeps the founder's "K" spirit but with golden ratio proportions, legible at 16px as at 2m on a trade show.

narrative.title: The editorial challenge
narrative.text: The vocabulary is ultra-specialized. "Balancing spreader beam," "30t hydraulic underwater winch," "DNV/LOLER compliance." The site had to remain accessible to technical buyers (who know) without scaring off more generalist buyers (military, industrialists). Solution: a systematic dual reading · an explicit title in plain French, a precise technical subtitle with the industry vocabulary.

narrative.title: Concrete impact
narrative.text: Loading time divided by 3 (optimized WordPress, WebP images, Cloudflare cache). Mobile-first responsive. Unified quote forms with pre-filled conditions by target sector. Client feedback: incoming first contacts become more qualified · prospects arrive having understood the specialization before contacting.

narrative.title: What I take from it
narrative.text: In a B2B niche market, art direction matters more than one might think. Technical credibility comes through graphic choices consistent with the trade · no unnecessary creative dev effects, but each element must signal "we know what we're talking about."

synapse.title: Synapse
synapse.text: Open-source plugin for Claude Code: syncs an AI assistant's memory across machines and projects instead of duplicating it.
synapse.context: Using Claude Code on 3 machines (personal, LR mission, laptop), I kept losing continuity: each machine had its own memory, none knew the others' context. Time-consuming and fragile manual duplication.
synapse.role: Concept, architecture, complete dev, tests, docs, publication. Solo.
synapse.stack: Node.js, TypeScript, Claude Code hooks, background git sync, smart local cache.
synapse.highlights: Sync collision detection (two machines writing at the same time). Named memory structure (feedback/project/user/reference). 283 tests, green CI from day 1. Published open-source from day 1.
synapse.outcome: Published on github.com/smaurier/claude-synapse. Plugin adopted daily on my 3 machines. Solid base for a future community.

detail.hero: A continuous AI memory across three machines.

narrative.title: The lived problem
narrative.text: In 2026, I use Claude Code daily on three machines: my personal setup at home, the one on mission at LR Technologies, a backup laptop. Each machine manages its own memory (user preferences, project context, validated feedback). Result: I repeat the same explanations to Claude on each machine, or worse, I manually copy memory files between machines with conflict risks. The "multiple assistants that don't know each other" pattern quickly becomes counterproductive.

narrative.title: Architecture chosen
narrative.text: Synapse is a plugin that bootstraps a Git-versioned memory structure, with automatic background sync on every significant change. Memory is typed: feedback (learned work rules), project (active project context), user (user profile), reference (pointers to external sources). Each entry has explicit YAML frontmatter, a short description, a type. A `[[name]]` linking system weaves entries together like a mini knowledge graph.

narrative.title: Technical choices
narrative.text: Node.js + TypeScript for cross-platform. Native Claude Code hooks (SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit) to intercept key moments without monkey-patching. Background Git sync via non-blocking `child_process`. Smart local cache to avoid unnecessary network round-trips. Sync collision detection: two machines write at the same time, Synapse attempts automatic per-entry merge, alerts the user on conflict.

narrative.title: Quality as obligation
narrative.text: 283 tests from the first public release, green CI, coverage > 80%. Why this rigor for a personal plugin? Because memory is precious · a bug that silently overwrites an entry is context lost that I won't recover. TDD here isn't dogma but a guarantee that memory doesn't corrupt itself.

narrative.title: Community opening
narrative.text: Published open-source from the first commit on github.com/smaurier/claude-synapse. Careful documentation, concrete examples, ADR (Architecture Decision Records) to trace choices. Ambition: that other multi-machine Claude Code users can bootstrap their own system. No business model, no premium · a tool solving a real problem for those who have it.

radar.title: Radar signaux · business intelligence in NestJS
radar.text: A watch engine over French open data (BODACC, INPI, trade press) that spots companies in the middle of raising funds. NestJS built test-first, SQLite, and an MCP server so an assistant can query it.
radar.context: A job search aimed at companies that hire after a funding round means crossing three sources that do not talk to each other: capital change notices published in the BODACC, amounts filed with the INPI, and the context given by the trade press. No free tool did it.
radar.role: Design, architecture, development, tests, deployment. Solo.
radar.stack: NestJS, TypeScript, SQLite (better-sqlite3), jest, Playwright + axe, MCP server, cron on GitHub Actions.
radar.highlights: First NestJS project built test-first end to end, with tests run against the real APIs. One cron engine for independent collectors. A read-only MCP server: signals are queried from an assistant rather than read off a dashboard.
radar.outcome: Public on GitHub, green CI, cron in production on GitHub Actions. Two modes shipped: Dev (funding rounds) and Freelance accessibility.

detail.hero: Three open sources, one NestJS engine, and signals you query in plain language.

narrative.title: The need
narrative.text: Applying to a company that has just raised funds means arriving before the job posting. The information exists and it is public, but it is scattered across three sources that do not know each other.

narrative.title: Three sources that do not talk
narrative.text: The BODACC publishes capital change notices, without amounts. The INPI holds the amount, without context. The trade press gives context, without structure. The engine crosses the three: a BODACC notice triggers the search for the INPI amount and a press article, and a signal is emitted only when the pieces agree.

narrative.title: NestJS, test-first
narrative.text: This is the first NestJS project built test-first end to end: modules, dependency injection, scheduler. The collectors were tested against the real APIs throughout, not against invented responses, because a public API changes without notice.

narrative.title: An MCP server to query it
narrative.text: Signals live in SQLite. Rather than a dashboard, a read-only MCP server exposes them: you ask an assistant, "which Lyon companies raised this month?", and it reads the database. The data stays where it is; the interface is the conversation.

narrative.title: What came out of it
narrative.text: The repository is public, continuous integration is green, and the cron runs in production on GitHub Actions. Two modes shipped: Dev, for funding rounds, and Freelance accessibility, which spots company websites worth auditing. The INPI client is clean enough to become a package of its own: that is next.

contact.title: Contact
contact.intro: A website project or an accessibility audit need? I'm available for new missions, let's talk.
contact.note: An idea worth exploring over coffee, or just want to talk tech, either works for me.

memoire.title: Teyolía · Memory
memoire.intro: Teyolía, one of the three entities that, in Nahua thought, make up a person: it lives in the heart, carries memory, and it's the one that travels to Mictlán after death. This page isn't a blog: it's an epitaph. What didn't survive building this site, kept rather than erased.

entries.title: The walk
entries.text: The stag advanced with the scroll, a technically correct stride cycle, unreadable over the few notches of a real scroll. Removed rather than tuned a third time: it added almost nothing for what it cost.

entries.title: The tree that wasn't from here
entries.text: A first accent of flora, photoreal texture, oversized, clashed with the rest of the scene, flat and vertex-colored. Replaced by a procedural ocotillo, truer to the pre-Columbian flora of central Mexico.

entries.title: The serpents
entries.text: Two attempts at a Xiuhcoatl for the loading veil, two admitted failures: a polyline too thin with no recognizable head, then a still-flawed trace. Removed while waiting for a real hand-drawn silhouette instead of one more procedural pass.

entries.title: The intro that dissolved
entries.text: The Piedra del Sol and the text dissolved into a cloud of embers before revealing the scene. A real vector technique (sampling around 250 SVG paths), but the effect didn't serve the story. Removed the day after it shipped.

entries.title: The calendar glyphs
entries.text: Five hybrid glyphs · Nahui Ollin for Center, Tonatiuh for East, Xochitl for South, Iztli for West, Ollin for North · drawn to animate cardinal transitions. Technically successful, but their codex fidelity made them sacred. Removed without regret, out of respect.

entries.title: The 2D petal curtain
entries.text: First attempt at inter-page transition: 1800 solid ellipses in mix-blend screen crossing the screen like confetti. Fast to code, cheap to watch. Replaced by native View Transitions API, more elegant.

entries.title: The slicing blade
entries.text: An HTML overlay that cut the screen into horizontal slices and slid them in the cardinal direction, like unfolding origami. Too mechanical, too readable as an effect, not organic enough for the site's cosmology.

entries.title: The 3D petal storm
entries.text: A rain of Three.js particles ejected from the stag during transition. Strong signal but confused reading: no clear focal point. Duplicated the existing petals' dispersion. Removed when View Transitions API took over.

entries.title: The brutal fade
entries.text: First iteration of transitions: router.push without burst, sharp WebGL canvas cut, next page appearing instantly. Technically correct, narratively disastrous. The stag teleported between worlds instead of crossing them.

entries.title: The sticky cursor
entries.text: First custom cursor attempt: lerp 0.02, a ring that took two seconds to catch up with the mouse. "Chewing gum" feel. Fixed to 0.15 to let the trail breathe without gluing it.

entries.title: The axial jade flame
entries.text: First Center Xiuhtecuhtli: a three-meter fire column crossing the stag. Strong signature, but it blinded the subject. Reduced to modest embers rising in a circle rather than a single dominant axis.

entries.title: The photorealistic god-rays
entries.text: First East Tonatiuh: GodRaysEffect post-processing shader with full volumetric sampling. Gorgeous at 60fps on dedicated GPU, catastrophic on mobile (30fps). Replaced with additive triangular planes, mesh-based, free to render.

memoire.creditNote: The cardinal motifs on this site (sun, flower, blade, spiral, quincunx) are stylized evocations inspired by Mesoamerican iconography, not reproductions of sacred glyphs. A family tribute to the living Nahua culture, for Elda and our daughters.

codex.title: Codex
codex.intro: A short manual for this site. The cosmogony that structures it, the human who writes it, the family that inhabits it.

cosmos.title: The five directions
cosmos.text: In Mesoamerican thought, the universe isn't read in four cardinal points but in five · the four horizons plus the center. Each direction carries its color, its god, its animal, its time of day. This site follows that plan.

directions.name: Center · Xiuhtecuhtli · jade
directions.text: The cosmic axis, the fire that burns without ever going out. Here is the home, the hub, the possible return.

directions.name: East · Tonatiuh · gold
directions.text: Dawn, the rising sun. Here are the services, what I offer to build with you.

directions.name: South · Huitzilopochtli · turquoise
directions.text: Noon, the warrior hummingbird. Here are the projects, what I've already carried through.

directions.name: West · Ehecatl · ash
directions.text: Dusk, the breath of wind. Here is contact, an open channel.

directions.name: North · Mictlantecuhtli · obsidian
directions.text: Night, the lord of the land of the dead. Here is Teyolía · Memory, what was kept rather than erased.

huitztlampa.title: Huitztlampa, the birth of the sun at Coatepec
huitztlampa.text: The South is Huitztlampa, the place of thorns, the region of the hummingbird. The Florentine Codex (Sahagún, book III) tells that at Coatepec, the serpent mountain, Coatlicue was sweeping the temple when a ball of feathers made her pregnant. Her children, Coyolxauhqui and the four hundred Huitznahua, the stars of the South, took the affront for a disgrace and climbed to kill her. Huitzilopochtli was born armed at the summit, struck Coyolxauhqui with the xiuhcoatl, the fire serpent, and scattered the four hundred. This is sunrise: every dawn, the moon is defeated and the stars fade. On this site, the Projects page replays that gesture. You arrive at night: the four hundred stars are thrown into the sky as you enter, the moon still keeps watch, high in the sky. As you scroll down, the hummingbirds, into which the warriors fallen in battle return, hunt the stars one by one · the sun rises in the east, red then white, and the moon sets. The xiuhcoatl prowls the sky, a mosaic of turquoise with embers at the joints, and at the top of the arc it strikes the stone, whose ring catches fire. Its tail carries the sign of the current year: in Nahuatl, xihuitl means turquoise, grass, comet and year at once. The fire serpent is also the serpent of time. In front of the stag, in the grass, stones write the year as monuments do: as many standing stones as the number, and a stele bearing the year-bearer glyph. What is attested: the blow of the xiuhcoatl, the defeated moon, the four hundred scattered, the count in dots. What is our reading: the serpent stiffening into a shaft (Seler saw in it the ray of the sun), the trembling mountain, the ring lifting, the turquoise flash, the stones catching fire.

mictlampa.title: Mictlampa, the descent to Mictlán
mictlampa.text: The North is Mictlampa, the place of the dead, the region of obsidian and night. Ordinary dead do not get there at once: according to Sahagún (book III) and the Codex Vaticanus A, the teyolía travels four years through nine layers before reaching Mictlantecuhtli and Mictecacihuatl. It crosses the river Chiconahuapan with the help of a dog, passes between two mountains that clash together, faces the obsidian wind of Itzehecayan that cuts like blades, then Temiminaloyan, where invisible hands shoot arrows. On this site, the Memory page is that descent. The stag stands in the black water of the tezcatl, the mirror: like Tezcatlipoca, the smoking mirror, it does not reflect, it reveals or it lies. Fog creeps in from the rim, obsidian blades sweep from east to west around the stag, and the deeper you go, the more arrows fall around him before dissolving into smoke. A path of cempasúchil, the flower that guides the dead home, stretches over the water toward the North. And Xolotl does pass, always, here: follow him with your eyes, he is the one who ferries souls across the river.

cihuatlampa.title: Cihuatlampa, the sun carried to its setting
cihuatlampa.text: The West is Cihuatlampa, the place of women, the region of dusk. Sahagún (book VI) tells that the sun, once at its zenith, is received by the Cihuateteo, the women who died in childbirth, deified like warriors fallen in battle, and that they carry it in a litter of quetzal feathers down to the sunset, where the people of Mictlán take it for the night. Book I names Ehecatl, the wind, the sweeper who opens the road for the rain gods. The Cihuateteo were no gentle figures: on certain days of the calendar they came down to the crossroads, where people dreaded their passing and left them papers and offerings. Their sculptures show them with faces painted in chalk, unbound hair, clawed hands, a plain skirt with a knotted belt. On this site, the Contact page is that evening road. You arrive in full daylight, and the further you go down, the further the sun falls toward the hills, on the right of the frame, while four black silhouettes carry its litter of feathers. When it enters the earth, they settle at the crossroads, facing the stag, and dance in the wind that sweeps everything toward the West. Papers remain on the ground, and butterflies escape from them: Sahagún (book III) says that women who died in childbirth come back as butterflies. What is attested: the litter of quetzal feathers, the descent to the crossroads, the papers and offerings, the chalk faces, the butterflies. What is our reading: the ash and coral colour (the sources give the West as white, the region of Quetzalcoatl), the dance, the visible wind, and the silhouettes themselves: the bodies are black and the faces stay patches of dimmed chalk, featureless, borrowing nothing from the faces of the sculptures.

tlahuizcalpan.title: Tlahuizcalpan, the darts of dawn
tlahuizcalpan.text: The East is Tlahuizcalpan, the house of dawn, the region of Tonatiuh. The sources call it red: our gold is a licence, gold being the metal of the sun. The Leyenda de los Soles tells that at Teotihuacan, after Nanahuatzin threw himself into the fire to become the sun, the sun stood still in the sky and burned everything. Tlahuizcalpantecuhtli, the lord of the house of dawn, who is Venus the morning star, grew angry and shot darts at him with his spear-thrower. He missed. The sun shot a dart back and turned him into Itztlacoliuhqui, the curved obsidian blade, the god of frost, the one through whom everything bent under the cold. Then the gods sacrificed themselves, and Ehecatl, the wind, finally pushed the sun along its road. The Anales de Cuauhtitlan add that Venus, on the day she reappears at dawn, wounds with her darts the old, the children, the lords or the rain, depending on the day sign. On this site, the Services page is that dawn. You arrive in a world caught in frost: the stag turned to glass, the Piedra under ice, time stopped, and he still breathing. At the edge the milpa lies flattened and small, killed by the cold: Itztlacoliuhqui is precisely the frost that kills plants. The moment the sun appears before you, the volley of darts leaves the morning star, the sun answers with a single dart falling from its shaft of light, and all the ice flies apart: the stag rears, the wind rises, a shaft of light falls on him, gold fills the carvings of the Piedra, the maize straightens and grows, and all that remains of the frost is a curved obsidian blade planted before him. If you scroll back up, the frost takes the screen for a few moments, and the world freezes again. What is attested: the motionless sun pushed by the wind, the darts of Venus, the dart in return and the metamorphosis into frost, the red East of Tonatiuh, the morning star that wounds. What is our reading: the whole world caught in ice, the explosion, the planted blade, the golden colour. And as in the West, the site watches the real sky: when Venus truly is the morning star, the volley is certain, otherwise one time in three.

suns.title: The four previous suns
suns.text: Before Nahui Ollin, four worlds lived and perished. Each left a lesson on how to die · and therefore how to live. Nahua cosmology does not think of creation as linear but as cycles that beget one another by collapsing. Our current sun is the fifth. It is mortal like the previous ones.

list.name: Nahui Ocelotl · 4 Jaguar
list.text: The first sun. Inhabitants were giants who lived on acorns. The world collapsed under jaguars who devoured the race. Fall by excess of strength.

list.name: Nahui Ehecatl · 4 Wind
list.text: The second sun, ruled by Quetzalcoatl. An immense wind blew the world away, humans transformed into monkeys still clinging to branches. Fall by lack of grounding.

list.name: Nahui Quiahuitl · 4 Fire Rain
list.text: The third sun, ruled by Tlaloc. A rain of fire burned the world, inhabitants transformed into turkeys who keep their red crest. Fall by celestial anger.

list.name: Nahui Atl · 4 Water
list.text: The fourth sun, ruled by Chalchiuhtlicue, Jade Skirt. A flood drowned the world, humans transformed into fish. Fall by tears held back too long.

ollin.title: Ollin, the tremor of the 5th sun
ollin.text: We live under Nahui Ollin, the sun of the four movements. Nahua prophecy says our world endures only as long as it trembles: when Ollin ceases, the earth stills one final time, Tonatiuh dies, the Tzitzimime descend. Every breath, every heartbeat, every touch is living proof of Ollin. On this site, when you press the mouse or tap the screen, a radial wave crosses the scene: that is Ollin manifesting. The stag Mazātl, messenger between worlds, feels the vibration before your eyes do. The four guardians awaken, the central fire redistributes. You are performing a ritual whose name you did not know. The historic Ollin glyph is a central circle bordered by four cardinal rays · the same five-point cross as the compass in the bottom right. Gesture and structure answer each other.

entities.title: The three entities of the Nahua being
entities.text: In Nahua thought, a person is not a single soul but three entities that coexist, each lodged in a part of the body. They separate at death and take distinct paths. Understanding this triptych is understanding why Teyolía names the Memory page of this site.

list.name: Teyolía · heart
list.text: The seat of memory, personality, intimate knowledge. It resides in the heart and, at death, travels to Mictlán after a four-year journey. It carries what you have been.

list.name: Tonalli · head
list.text: The vital force tied to the day of birth in the tonalpohualli calendar. It resides in the head and radiates like a heat. It can escape during intense fright · hence the rituals to recall the tonalli after a shock.

list.name: Ihíyotl · liver
list.text: The breath, the passions, the desires. It resides in the liver and belly. If unmastered, it can escape and affect others · moral illnesses come from there.

xolotl.title: Xolotl, the dog of dusk
xolotl.text: Twin brother of Quetzalcoatl, Xolotl is the dog who guides souls to Mictlán after death, and he is also the evening Venus, who follows the sun under the earth. Skeletal, silent, he crosses the worlds without ever stopping · except for those who know how to look. On this site, he always passes in the North (the Memory page, the natural road to Mictlán). In the West, he obeys the real sky: when Venus truly shines after sunset, he comes without fail once the sun has entered the earth, and the evening star lights up above the sunset; the rest of the year, one time in three. Never on the home page, nor in the East, nor in the South. If you saw him pass, the scene judged you worthy of his attention.

totem.title: The stag, Mazātl
totem.text: The nahual is that essence which reveals itself in its true animal form. I chose the stag over the eagle or the jaguar · deliberately avoiding the "Aztec imagery" cliché to stay in the more discreet register of presence: messenger between worlds, associated with grace, vigilance, and the ability to hide one's true nature from others.

human.title: Who writes
human.text: Sylvain Maurier, senior frontend developer based in Lyon. Ten years shipping interfaces (React, Next.js, Vue, React Native), an ongoing specialization in digital accessibility (RGAA, certification exam October 23, 2026). A simple thread: accessibility is coded, not just audited. PDF reports don't change the world, fix code does.

family.title: The family that inhabits this site
family.text: Nahual is a French-Mexican project as much as a personal one. Elda, my partner, is Mexican, a native Spanish speaker, a teacher. Léopoldine is our daughter, born in Lyon. Alondra is her older sister, adopted in Mexico. Nahua cosmogony isn't a randomly chosen exotic backdrop · it's a family heritage I'm still learning, with the respect that requires.

respect.title: On cultural appropriation
respect.text: This site pays tribute to a living culture, not a museum. The cardinal motifs (sun, flower, blade, spiral, quincunx) are stylized evocations inspired by Mesoamerican iconography, not reproductions of sacred glyphs. Calendar glyphs, the Fejérváry-Mayer codex, the Piedra del Sol are deliberately absent from decorative elements without context. The red line is simple: celebrate what is public, leave what is sacred to those who hold it.

refs.title: What inspired me
refs.text: Sacred Labs and Joseph Santamaria for WebGL sobriety, Lusion and Immersive Garden for web cinematography, Bruno Simon for the narrative daring of a 3D portfolio. The Fejérváry-Mayer and Borgia codices for the cosmological structure. Miguel León-Portilla's and Alfredo López Austin's studies for the depth of Nahua philosophy. Thanks to Elda for the patience, to Léo for the micro-naps that saved a few deadlines.

sources.title: Sources
sources.text: Everything this Codex claims comes from somewhere. Here is where to read it, online when a digitization exists, and where to see it or buy it for real.

list.name: Florentine Codex · Sahagún, around 1577
list.text: Bernardino de Sahagún, Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España. Book I: Ehecatl, sweeper of the road of the rain gods. Book III: the birth of Huitzilopochtli at Coatepec (chapter 1), the nine stages toward Mictlán and the women who died in childbirth returning as butterflies (appendix). Book VI: the Cihuateteo carrying the sun in a litter of quetzal feathers. Book VII: the sun created at Teotihuacan, and Xolotl. Book VII, chapter 2: the sun created at Teotihuacan, motionless until the gods' sacrifice and Ehecatl's breath.

online.label: Digital Florentine Codex, Getty Research Institute, Book III (Nahuatl, Spanish, English)
French translation by Jourdanet and Siméon, Paris, 1880, on archive.org

list.physical: Original at the Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Florence. Editions: Anderson and Dibble, Florentine Codex, University of Utah Press, 12 volumes; Porrúa, Mexico City, Sepan cuantos series, 1999, ISBN 9684322658.

list.name: Codex Vaticanus A · Codex Ríos, around 1570 to 1589
list.text: The layers of Mictlán painted folio by folio, and the previous suns. The pictorial source of the descent to the North.

online.label: DigiVatLib, Vatican Apostolic Library, Vat. lat. 3738

list.physical: Vatican Apostolic Library, Rome. Facsimile: Akademische Druck- und Verlagsanstalt, Graz, 1979.

list.name: Codex Chimalpopoca · Leyenda de los Soles
list.text: The four suns, how each ended, and Nahui Ollin. The five suns story in this Codex comes from here. The darts of Tlahuizcalpantecuhtli against the motionless sun, and his metamorphosis into Itztlacoliuhqui, the frost: that is the story of the Services page.

online.label: John Bierhorst, History and Mythology of the Aztecs: The Codex Chimalpopoca, digital lending on archive.org

list.physical: John Bierhorst, University of Arizona Press, 1992, ISBN 9780816502455.

list.name: Codex Borgia
list.text: A divinatory manuscript, one of the cosmological structures behind this site. Plate 53: Tlahuizcalpantecuhtli and his darts. The figure is not copied on the site: there, the god is the star itself.
list.physical: Vatican Apostolic Library, Rome. Annotated edition: Anders, Jansen and Reyes García, Fondo de Cultura Económica, Mexico City, 1993, ISBN 9789681641542.

list.name: Cihuateotl · Mexica sculpture, 1400 to 1521
list.text: One of the deified women of the West, in stone: kneeling, arms raised at the sides of the chest, clawed hands, unbound hair, a plain skirt with a knotted belt. It is the source for the pose and the garment of the bearers on the Contact page, never for their face.

online.label: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, 00.5.30, online record

list.physical: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, gallery 360. The four Cihuateteo found together in Mexico City are at the Museo Nacional de Antropología, Mexica hall.

list.name: Codex Fejérváry-Mayer
list.text: Its first page, the four directions around the centre, is the plan of this site.

online.label: World Museum record, National Museums Liverpool

list.name: The Coyolxauhqui stone
list.text: The monolith found in 1978 at the foot of the Templo Mayor, the dismembered moon at the bottom of Coatepec. The gesture the Projects page replays.
list.physical: Museo del Templo Mayor, Seminario 8, Centro Histórico, Mexico City.

list.name: The Piedra del Sol
list.text: The Ollin glyph at the centre, the four suns around it: the compass at the bottom right descends from it.
list.physical: Museo Nacional de Antropología, Chapultepec, Mexico City.

list.name: Alfredo López Austin · Cuerpo humano e ideología
list.text: The reference study on teyolía, tonalli and ihíyotl, the three entities of the Nahua person.
list.physical: UNAM, Instituto de Investigaciones Antropológicas, Mexico City, 1980. In English: The Human Body and Ideology, University of Utah Press, 1988, ISBN 9780874802603.

list.name: Miguel León-Portilla · La filosofía náhuatl
list.text: Nahua thought read by one of its own: the tlamatinimeh, time, the suns.
list.physical: UNAM, Mexico City, 1956, reprinted since. In French: La pensée aztèque, Seuil, Paris, 1985, ISBN 9782020067126.

list.name: Nahuatl dictionaries
list.text: For xihuitl, tezcatl, Huitztlampa and every glossed word in this Codex.
list.physical: Frances Karttunen, An Analytical Dictionary of Nahuatl, University of Oklahoma Press, 1992, ISBN 9780806124216.

accessibilite.title: Accessibility statement
accessibilite.intro: Nahual is committed to making its site accessible under the French General Accessibility Improvement Reference (RGAA) version 4.1.

sections.title: Conformance state
sections.text: This site is partially compliant with RGAA 4.1. A full audit is planned after the 2026 redesign stabilizes.

sections.title: Non-accessible content
sections.text: The interactive 3D scene (WebGL canvas) is decorative: main textual content (titles, texts, links) is accessible to assistive technologies. prefers-reduced-motion is respected.

sections.title: Statement drafting
sections.text: This statement was drafted on August 28, 2026 based on self-assessment. An external audit is planned after obtaining RGAA certification (October 2026).

sections.title: Feedback and contact
sections.text: To report an access issue or obtain an alternative version of content, contact bonjour@nahual.fr. If no response within 60 days, contact the French Rights Defender: https://www.defenseurdesdroits.fr.

sections.title: Keyboard shortcuts
sections.text: Alt+Up/Right/Down/Left Arrow: direct cardinal navigation (up=Memory North, right=Services East, down=Projects South, left=Contact West). WASD (QWERTY) or ZQSD (AZERTY) · independent of physical layout · same cardinal grid: W/Z=Memory, D=Services, S=Projects, A/Q=Contact, C=Home (Center). Escape: return home. Scene controls (single letters): H hides or shows the text, F full screen, T contemplation (the text fades out, the scene settles on Tenochtitlan's real time, the actual height of the sun over Mexico City, then plays the whole day in a loop while the camera slowly orbits; any gesture stops it and brings the text back as it was), P photo of the scene, L copies the link to this moment, E eco mode. These shortcuts obey the same switch as the others.

sections.title: Gamepad shortcuts
sections.text: A USB or Bluetooth gamepad (Xbox, PlayStation, standard) is auto-detected. D-pad: cardinal navigation (up=Memory, right=Services, down=Projects, left=Contact). A/B buttons (Xbox) or Cross/Circle (PlayStation): return home.

confidentialite.title: Privacy policy
confidentialite.intro: This site complies with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the French Data Protection Act.

sections.title: Data collected
sections.text: No data is collected without your explicit action. Sending a message via the email shown on the Contact page is the only entry point: the information provided (email, message content) is used solely to reply.

sections.title: Cookies and trackers
sections.text: This site does not use tracking cookies or third-party analytics tools (no Google Analytics, no Meta Pixel). Only local storage (localStorage) is used to remember your sound preference (on/off) and whether you've already seen certain animations. This data stays in your browser and is never transmitted.

sections.title: Retention
sections.text: Messages received by email are kept for the time needed to process them, then archived in the responsible party's personal mailbox for future reference. You can request their deletion at any time.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.text: Under GDPR, you have the right to access, rectify, erase, and port your data. Contact: bonjour@nahual.fr.

credits.title: Credits and attributions
credits.intro: This site uses resources created by others. Recognition and gratitude.

sections.title: 3D models
sections.text: The stag and part of the flora come from Quaternius open-source packs (CC0 license). Xolotl (the dog-brother of Quetzalcoatl who sometimes crosses the scene) uses the Xoloitzcuintle model by Nyilonelycompany, purchased on Fab.com, tinted obsidian. Complementary models (ocotillo, vines) are procedurally generated. The cempasúchil flowers of the North are modelled procedurally. The hummingbirds of the South use the Hummingbird model from Poly by Google (CC BY 3.0 licence), recoloured per species; the fire serpent Xiuhcoatl was modelled by Blender script for this site. The South daytime sky is the photograph “Kloofendal 48d Partly Cloudy (Pure Sky)” by Greg Zaal and Jarod Guest, Poly Haven, CC0 licence, tinted for the scene. The bearers of the West use a Quaternius model (CC0 licence), dressed for this site. The nopal `nopal-google.glb` comes from the Poly by Google archive, like the hummingbird, and is credited as CC BY 3.0 accordingly. A file-by-file record is kept in the repository (docs/credits-modeles.md).

sections.title: Fonts
sections.text: Geist Sans and Geist Mono, created by Vercel (SIL Open Font license).

sections.title: Software libraries

sections.title: Inspirations
sections.text: Sacred Labs (Joseph Santamaria), Lusion, Immersive Garden, Bruno Simon, Codrops. Fejérváry-Mayer and Borgia codices for cosmology. Miguel León-Portilla's and Alfredo López Austin's studies for the depth of Nahua philosophy.

sections.title: Cultural recognition
sections.text: This site is a tribute to the living Nahua culture, not a museum. For Elda, Alondra, Léopoldine, and all who carry this memory.
